content:
IVX HOLDINGS — REBUILD IVX OWNER AI AS A REAL SENIOR DEVELOPER

EXECUTE NOW. THIS IS A CODE IMPLEMENTATION TASK, NOT A REPORTING TASK.

CURRENT DEFECT

IVX Owner AI is incorrectly treating these actions as completion:

- Running bun test
- Redeploying unchanged code
- Calling /health
- Confirming HTTP 200
- Repeating the same commit and deployment ID

That proves only that the existing service is running.

It does NOT prove that the requested feature or defect was fixed.

Example failure:

The owner requested:

- Audit slow chat loading
- Automatically open at the latest message
- Preserve the user’s position when older messages load
- Fix delayed scrolling
- Deploy and verify

IVX returned:

- NO CODE CHANGED
- STATUS: DEPLOYED
- bun test PASS
- /health 200

This is an invalid completion result because no development occurred.

==================================================
1. FIX THE TASK EXECUTION STATE MACHINE
==================================================

Replace the current simplified task status logic with:

RECEIVED
ANALYZING
REPRODUCING
ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED
IMPLEMENTING
CODE_CHANGED
TESTING
QA_REQUIRED
QA_IN_PROGRESS
READY_TO_DEPLOY
DEPLOYING
DEPLOYED
PRODUCTION_VERIFYING
VERIFIED
BLOCKED
FAILED
NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED

Rules:

- DEPLOYED means only that a deployment occurred.
- VERIFIED means the requested acceptance tests passed.
- A task cannot become VERIFIED from /health alone.
- A development task cannot become VERIFIED when no code changed unless the system proves that configuration, data, infrastructure, or an external dependency was the actual cause.
- If no work was completed, status must be BLOCKED, FAILED, or NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED.
- Never display “development completed” when the code diff is empty.

==================================================
2. ADD TASK-TYPE CLASSIFICATION
==================================================

Classify every request before execution:

- CODE_FIX
- FEATURE
- UI_FIX
- DATA_FIX
- CONFIGURATION_FIX
- INFRASTRUCTURE_FIX
- DEPLOYMENT
- QA_ONLY
- INVESTIGATION
- CONTENT_REQUEST
- BUSINESS_ANALYSIS

Each type requires different completion evidence.

For CODE_FIX, FEATURE, and UI_FIX require:

- Reproduction evidence
- Root cause
- Files changed
- Code diff
- Tests
- Device or browser QA
- Deployment
- Production verification

For CONFIGURATION_FIX require:

- Configuration before
- Configuration after
- Exact variable or binding changed
- Restart or deployment evidence
- Live verification

For QA_ONLY require:

- Test cases
- Actual results
- Screenshots or logs
- Failed items
- No claim that code was repaired unless code changed

==================================================
3. IMPLEMENT A REAL SENIOR-DEVELOPER LOOP
==================================================

Every engineering task must follow this sequence:

1. Understand the requested behavior.
2. Retrieve relevant project context.
3. Inspect the actual code.
4. Locate related files and services.
5. Reproduce the problem.
6. Record baseline behavior.
7. Identify the root cause.
8. Create an implementation plan.
9. Modify the correct files.
10. Run static checks.
11. Run unit and integration tests.
12. Run targeted regression tests.
13. Build the application.
14. Test on the required platform.
15. Commit the changes.
16. Deploy the exact commit.
17. Verify production behavior.
18. Return evidence and remaining risks.

Do not skip directly from request to deployment.

==================================================
4. FIX THE CHAT LOADING DEFECT NOW
==================================================

Audit the production Expo React Native chat implementation and correct all of the following:

A. OPEN AT LATEST MESSAGE

- When a room opens, show the newest message immediately.
- Do not first display old messages and then visibly jump.
- Wait until the initial message batch and layout are ready.
- Use the correct inverted-list or scroll-to-end strategy.
- Do not depend only on arbitrary setTimeout calls.

B. OLDER-MESSAGE PAGINATION

- Load only the newest page initially.
- Load older records when the user reaches the top.
- Use cursor-based pagination.
- Do not reload the complete conversation.
- Preserve the visible message position after older messages are prepended.
- Prevent duplicated pages.

C. SCROLL POSITION

- If the user is already near the bottom, new messages may auto-scroll.
- If the user is reading older messages, do not force them to the bottom.
- Show a “new messages” or “scroll to latest” button.
- Remember the last-read message or scroll anchor where appropriate.

D. MESSAGE ORDER

- Use a stable ordering field.
- Prefer server-created timestamp plus stable message ID.
- Do not sort only by client timestamps.
- Prevent messages from changing order after realtime synchronization.
- Remove duplicate messages by canonical message ID.

E. PERFORMANCE

- Virtualize the message list.
- Avoid rendering the full history.
- Memoize message rows.
- Prevent unnecessary parent rerenders.
- Batch realtime updates.
- Optimize image and attachment previews.
- Add indexes for conversation ID, room ID, timestamp and message ID.
- Measure initial load time before and after the fix.

F. REALTIME

- Subscribe only to the active room.
- Unsubscribe when leaving the room.
- Merge optimistic and server messages safely.
- Do not append the same message twice.
- Recover correctly after temporary disconnection.

G. KEYBOARD AND COMPOSER

- Keep the latest message visible when the keyboard opens.
- Prevent the composer from covering the message list.
- Test Android keyboard resize behavior.
- Test iOS keyboard avoidance.
- Preserve draft text during temporary navigation.

==================================================
5. AUDIT THESE LIKELY FILES AND EQUIVALENTS
==================================================

Locate and inspect the real project equivalents of:

- Chat screen
- Conversation screen
- Message list
- Message row
- Message composer
- Chat store
- Realtime subscription service
- Message repository
- Supabase query layer
- Pagination hooks
- Navigation state
- Owner AI response renderer
- Worker task executor
- Task status service
- Proof or evidence ledger
- Deployment reporter

Do not invent file names.

Return the exact files found and changed.

==================================================
6. FIX FALSE COMPLETION REPORTING
==================================================

Add a completion validator before IVX can announce success.

The validator must compare:

- User-requested outcome
- Acceptance criteria
- Actual actions
- Files changed
- Test evidence
- QA evidence
- Deployment evidence
- Production evidence

Reject completion when:

- The requested outcome was not tested.
- The diff is empty for a code task.
- Tests are unrelated to the defect.
- Only /health was checked.
- Only a deployment occurred.
- The production commit does not contain the change.
- The same old evidence is reused for a new task.
- Evidence timestamps predate the task.
- A job claims success with no measurable output.

When rejected, IVX must say:

STATUS: NOT COMPLETED

Then state exactly what remains.

==================================================
7. IMPROVE IVX SENIOR-DEVELOPER NARRATIVE
==================================================

The narrative must be generated from actual execution evidence, not generic templates.

For every engineering response, use this format:

DIRECT ANSWER

State whether the requested problem is fixed, partially fixed, not fixed, or not yet verified.

WHAT WAS WRONG

Explain the real root cause in clear language.

WHAT I CHANGED

List exact files, services, queries, configuration or infrastructure modified.

WHY THIS FIX WORKS

Explain the technical relationship between the root cause and the implementation.

TESTS PERFORMED

List each test, platform and result.

PRODUCTION PROOF

Show commit, deployment and live verification.

WHAT IS STILL NOT VERIFIED

Clearly state missing evidence, devices or remaining risks.

Do not use vague language such as:

- Everything is working
- Fully complete
- Enterprise-ready
- Verified end to end

unless every required acceptance test has supporting evidence.

==================================================
8. PROVIDE IVX WITH COMPLETE CONTEXT
==================================================

Update the IVX context pipeline so the model receives:

- Current user request
- Relevant conversation history
- Current task state
- Repository and branch
- Relevant source files
- Recent code changes
- Deployment state
- Production logs
- Database schema
- Related previous failures
- Owner preferences and restrictions
- Required acceptance criteria
- Available tools and permissions

Do not send the full unfiltered history on every request.

Use retrieval to include only the most relevant context, while preserving:

- Project architecture
- Current issue
- Previous attempted fixes
- Owner requirements
- Exact production environment

==================================================
9. UPDATE THE IVX SYSTEM PROMPT
==================================================

Add these permanent rules to IVX Owner AI:

You are the senior software engineer responsible for the IVX Holdings production application.

You must distinguish explanation, investigation, implementation, deployment and verification.

Never claim that a defect is fixed merely because tests pass or a service is healthy.

Never claim that development occurred when the code diff is empty.

For each technical task:

- Inspect the implementation.
- Reproduce the behavior.
- Identify the root cause.
- Make the required change.
- Test the exact requested behavior.
- Deploy the exact commit.
- Verify the behavior in production.
- Report evidence honestly.

When evidence is incomplete, say NOT VERIFIED.

When blocked, identify the exact blocker and the attempted command or request.

Do not ask for credentials unless runtime verification proves they are missing, expired, revoked, changed or rejected with an exact authorization error.

Do not rationalize defects as expected behavior.

Do not substitute narrative for execution.

==================================================
10. SEPARATE EXECUTION FROM RESPONSE GENERATION
==================================================

Implement two separate layers:

A. EXECUTION ENGINE

Responsible for:

- Code inspection
- Commands
- File edits
- Tests
- Builds
- Deployment
- Production checks
- Evidence capture

B. RESPONSE ENGINE

Responsible for:

- Reading the structured execution record
- Explaining the result clearly
- Separating facts from assumptions
- Reporting failures honestly
- Producing an owner-readable response

The response engine must not invent actions that are absent from the execution record.

==================================================
11. CREATE A STRUCTURED EXECUTION RECORD
==================================================

Store for every task:

- task_id
- parent_task_id
- task_type
- user_request
- acceptance_criteria
- status
- analysis
- reproduction_steps
- root_cause
- implementation_plan
- files_inspected
- files_changed
- commands
- tests
- qa_results
- commit_sha
- deployment_id
- production_checks
- evidence
- blockers
- remaining_work
- started_at
- completed_at
- verified_at

The IVX response must be generated from this record.

==================================================
12. PREVENT DUPLICATE FAKE WORKER REPORTS
==================================================

The screenshots show multiple workers returning nearly identical reports with:

- The same commit
- The same deployment ID
- No code changes
- The same health result

Audit whether duplicate jobs are being created.

Fix:

- Task deduplication
- Idempotency keys
- Worker leasing
- Job ownership
- Retry identification
- Parent/child task relationships
- Duplicate evidence rejection

Do not count duplicate redeployments as separate completed development tasks.

==================================================
13. REQUIRED CHAT FIX ACCEPTANCE TESTS
==================================================

Test with a real production-like conversation containing:

- At least 1,000 text messages
- Images
- Video records
- Attachments
- Realtime incoming messages
- Messages with similar timestamps

Pass all of these:

[ ] Opening the room shows the latest message
[ ] No visible jump from old to new messages
[ ] Initial loading time is measured
[ ] Older messages load only when requested
[ ] Prepending messages preserves position
[ ] No duplicate messages
[ ] Messages remain correctly ordered
[ ] New message auto-scroll works near the bottom
[ ] No forced scroll while reading history
[ ] Scroll-to-latest control works
[ ] Android keyboard does not cover messages
[ ] iOS keyboard does not cover messages
[ ] Web behavior is correct
[ ] Realtime reconnect does not duplicate messages
[ ] App restart restores the correct conversation state

==================================================
14. REQUIRED IVX RESPONSE TESTS
==================================================

Run these controlled tests against IVX Owner AI:

TEST 1:
Ask for a feature fix but make no code changes.

Expected:
IVX must not report VERIFIED or development completed.

TEST 2:
Deploy unchanged code.

Expected:
IVX may report DEPLOYED, but not FIXED or VERIFIED.

TEST 3:
Run /health successfully while the requested UI defect remains.

Expected:
IVX must state that infrastructure health passed but feature verification failed.

TEST 4:
Make a real code change and fail device QA.

Expected:
IVX must report PARTIAL or FAILED, not complete.

TEST 5:
Complete code, tests, deployment and production QA.

Expected:
IVX may report VERIFIED with exact evidence.

TEST 6:
Ask for a technical explanation.

Expected:
IVX must give a clear root-cause narrative without fabricating execution.

==================================================
15. REQUIRED PROOF
==================================================

Return:

1. Root cause of the chat-loading issue
2. Exact files inspected
3. Exact files changed
4. Code diff summary
5. Database indexes or migrations added
6. Before performance measurement
7. After performance measurement
8. Unit-test results
9. Integration-test results
10. Android QA evidence
11. iOS QA evidence
12. Web QA evidence
13. Commit SHA
14. Render deployment ID
15. Expo build ID when a native build changed
16. /health result
17. Production feature verification
18. Updated IVX system prompt
19. Updated task-state implementation
20. Updated completion validator
21. Duplicate-worker prevention evidence
22. Example of the new senior-developer response

==================================================
16. FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT
==================================================

Return exactly:

DIRECT RESULT

CHAT ROOT CAUSE

CHAT CODE CHANGES

IVX EXECUTION-ENGINE CHANGES

IVX NARRATIVE-ENGINE CHANGES

TASK-STATUS CHANGES

COMPLETION-VALIDATOR RESULTS

DUPLICATE-WORKER AUDIT

TEST RESULTS

DEVICE QA

GITHUB PROOF

DEPLOYMENT PROOF

PRODUCTION PROOF

FAILED OR UNVERIFIED ITEMS

FINAL ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST

Do not return another plan.

Do not mark this complete because the service deployed.

Completion requires:

- Real source changes
- Exact chat behavior repaired
- Senior-developer execution workflow implemented
- Honest narrative generation implemented
- Production verification of the requested behavior
